source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Cushing's triad in increased ICP consists of:
questions.rationale: Cushing's triad is a late sign of rising ICP.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Increased ICP (PDF p. 423)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which action helps prevent increased ICP?
questions.rationale: Avoid straining and coughing; keep HOB elevated about 30 degrees.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ICP Nursing Management (PDF p. 423)
questions.quote: Prevent Valsalva Maneuver and the activities that may increase ICP

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drug is given to reduce cerebral edema?
questions.rationale: Osmotic diuretic mannitol reduces cerebral edema.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ICP Nursing Management (PDF p. 423)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A transient ischemic attack typically lasts:
questions.rationale: TIA: neurologic deficit typically under 1 hour, a warning of stroke.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CVA (PDF p. 423)
questions.quote: Neurologic deficit typically lasting less than 1 hour

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Cardiogenic embolic stroke is most often associated with:
questions.rationale: Atrial fibrillation produces emboli.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Ischemic Stroke (PDF p. 424)
questions.quote: Associated with dysrhythmias usually atrial fibrillation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the major risk factor for stroke?
questions.rationale: Hypertension is the major risk factor.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CVA Risk Factors (PDF p. 424)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The most common cause of subarachnoid hemorrhage is:
questions.rationale: A leaking aneurysm near the Circle of Willis or AVM.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hemorrhagic Stroke (PDF p. 424)
questions.quote: Most common cause is a leaking aneurysm

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client after stroke can understand but cannot form words. This is:
questions.rationale: Expressive (Broca's): cannot form words; receptive: cannot understand.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Communication Loss (PDF p. 425)
questions.quote: Unable to form words that are understandable

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which is typical of a right hemispheric stroke?
questions.rationale: Right stroke: left weakness, spatial deficits, impulsivity, unawareness of deficits.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hemispheric Strokes (PDF p. 425)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with homonymous hemianopsia should be taught to:
options: Turn head toward the lost field
questions.rationale: Scanning toward the visual loss compensates; approach from the unaffected side.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CVA Nursing (PDF p. 425)
questions.quote: turn head in the direction of visual loss

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When feeding a client with dysphagia after stroke, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Check gag reflex, sit upright, give soft foods on the unaffected side.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CVA Nursing (PDF p. 426)
questions.quote: Place food in unaffected side of the mouth

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which positioning prevents a common complication in a hemiplegic client?
questions.rationale: Place a pillow in the axilla to prevent adduction and contracture.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CVA Nursing (PDF p. 425)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client with meningococcal meningitis is kept on respiratory isolation for:
questions.rationale: Droplet precautions until 24 hours of effective antibiotics.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Meningitis (PDF p. 426)
questions.quote: Enforce respiratory isolation for 24 hours after initiation of antibiotic medication

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which test confirms bacterial meningitis?
questions.rationale: CSF Gram stain and culture via lumbar puncture.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Meningitis (PDF p. 426)
questions.quote: Bacterial culture & Gram Staining of CSF & blood through lumbar puncture

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which environment is best for a client with meningitis?
questions.rationale: Photophobia and irritability; keep room dark and quiet.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Meningitis Nursing (PDF p. 426)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the most common cause of encephalitis?
questions.rationale: HSV is most common; treated with acyclovir.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Encephalitis (PDF p. 427)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A child stares blankly for a few seconds several times a day. This is:
questions.rationale: Absence (petit mal) seizures: brief staring, common in children.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Seizures (PDF p. 428)
questions.quote: Manifested by a period of staring for several seconds

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client picks at clothing and smacks lips with loss of awareness. This is:
questions.rationale: Complex partial (psychomotor): automatisms with loss of consciousness.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Partial Seizures (PDF p. 428)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During a tonic-clonic seizure, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Ease to floor, protect head, loosen clothing; never restrain or insert objects.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Seizure Nursing (PDF p. 428)
questions.quote: Protect the head of the patient

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After a seizure, the client should be positioned:
questions.rationale: Side-lying prevents aspiration; keep suction available.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Seizure Nursing (PDF p. 428)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What are the earliest signs of myasthenia gravis?
questions.rationale: Ocular weakness (ptosis, diplopia) appears first.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Myasthenia Gravis (PDF p. 429)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Improved muscle strength after edrophonium injection indicates:
questions.rationale: Positive Tensilon test; atropine is the antidote.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tensilon Test (PDF p. 429)
questions.quote: Positive (+) = resolved facial muscle weakness & ptosis

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When should pyridostigmine be given to a client with myasthenia gravis?
questions.rationale: Give before meals for chewing and swallowing strength, on schedule.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, MG Nursing (PDF p. 429)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drug class should be avoided in myasthenia gravis?
questions.rationale: Avoid muscle relaxants, barbiturates, morphine, tranquilizers, neomycin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, MG Medications to Avoid (PDF p. 429)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Cholinergic crisis in myasthenia gravis is caused by:
questions.rationale: Cholinergic crisis: excess anticholinesterase; myasthenic crisis: undermedication.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cholinergic Crisis (PDF p. 429)
